name: Kigali International Airport
before:
Rwanda's way in, and a compact one. Three terminals share the site: the main two storey building, the original single storey terminal now used for VIPs, and a cargo terminal. The main terminal takes six small to mid sized aircraft at a time and can handle a 747 when one comes. Two helicopter pads sit on the south side of the runway.

RwandAir has its head office on the top floor, which tells you how central this airport is to the national carrier. Three other airlines are based here: Akagera Aviation flies helicopters, Tempus Jet runs American charters and Nexus Aero is a Saudi VIP operator.

There is free Wi-Fi in the waiting area. The airport was ranked seventh best regional airport in Africa in 2014, largely on the strength of its emergency response, with a Category Nine fire service rated second best against international aviation standards. The tarmac and support systems were last upgraded in 2002.
after:
Rwanda's main way in by air. It is RwandAir's hub, and the airline has its head office on the top floor of the main building. Akagera Aviation is based here too and runs helicopter transfers within Rwanda.

Between 2014 and 2017 more than 30 million US dollars went into a new apron, three taxiways and a hangar. Works begun in September 2019 added another apron for 18 aircraft and an arrivals terminal. Its fire and rescue service is rated Category 9.

claims.note: Was 'Rwanda's way in'; 'by air' added because Rwanda also has land borders. Wikipedia calls it Rwanda's principal international airport. The Rwanda Development Board's own 'Getting Here' section names this airport and no other. The Rwanda Airports Company lists one other international airport, Kamembe, near the Congo border, where the FCDO advises against all but essential travel.

claims.claim: Held back: the FCDO reports Ebola health screening at Kigali International Airport
claims.why: Held back: replaces nothing in the old text. The FCDO's Rwanda advice (updated 4 September 2026, still current on 23 September) says that, in response to the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, the Government of Rwanda has introduced health screening at Kigali International Airport, and that the measures may change at short notice. An attributed statement; for Andy to add if he wants it.
